fields.meta_description: Build a personal injury intake form that counts down to the filing deadline, checks every name for conflicts and totals medical bills. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Personal Injury Intake Form That Starts the Case File
fields.hero_description: Describe your case types and your state's filing limit. Emergent builds the personal injury intake form, a case database behind it and alerts for the attorney who needs to act.
fields.explore_cta: Build My Personal Injury Intake Form
fields.features_heading: What a Personal Injury Intake Form Collects
fields.features_subheading: Every section feeds a job someone at the firm does in the first week of a case.
fields.feature_1:
A filing deadline saved on submit

Ask for the date of the incident and the state where it happened. The form applies the limit your firm sets for that state and shows every intake with its days left to file.
fields.feature_2:
Names your conflict search can read

Put the other driver and the property owner in fields of their own, and each witness too. Staff run every name against the client list before anyone calls the new person back.
fields.feature_3:
Treatment logged one provider at a time

Add a row for each hospital or clinic with visit dates and the amount billed. The form totals the bills on submit and gives the paralegal a ready list for records requests.
fields.feature_4:
Both insurers on the first page

Ask for the client's own carrier and the other party's carrier, each with its claim number and the adjuster's name. Staff open the claim file without a second phone call.
fields.feature_5:
Photos and reports filed with the case

Accept scene photos straight from a phone, plus the police report and any bills already received. Each upload lands in storage you own, filed under the intake it came with.
fields.feature_6:
Code your firm can take anywhere

Export the form and its database to your GitHub repository. Run it on your own servers, or have a developer connect it to the case management software the firm uses.

fields.usecase_heading: Personal Injury Intake by Case Type
fields.tab_content_1:
When 61 days remain, an attorney hears within the hour

Kestrel Injury Law practices in Texas, where the limit for a personal injury suit is two years. Ruth Adler slipped in a grocery aisle and enters the date of her fall. The form saves her deadline and shows 61 days left. Any intake under 90 days reaches lead attorney Marcus Bell in Slack on submit.
fields.tab_content_2:
Held for review when the other driver is a client

Hollis Grant checks every name on a crash intake against its client list. Nina Ford was rear-ended at a light and names the other driver and his insurer. The search matches the driver, Evan Marsh, to a current client in an unrelated matter. Her intake waits for the managing partner.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each provider turns into its own records request

Owen Price was bitten by a neighbor's dog and lists four providers. The emergency room billed $2,860, urgent care $340, a plastic surgeon $750 and the pharmacy $85. The form totals $4,035. The paralegal gets one records request per provider, with the dog owner's address on file.
fields.tab_content_4:
Who else was there decides which team

Harbor Point Law sorts injuries at work by whether anyone outside the employer was involved. A delivery van from another company backed into Luis Moreno at a loading dock. His intake goes to the injury team and the workers' comp group. A coworker hurt lifting a pallet goes to workers' comp alone.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Personal Injury Intake Form
fields.howto_description: Start from the questions your attorneys repeat on first calls, then decide which answers should move a case before anyone calls back.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask the date and the place first
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull the last ten intakes your staff took by phone and mark every question an attorney had to ask again on the first call. Those repeat questions belong on the form. Anything nobody looked at after the first week can come off.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Start with the date and the place of the incident, since your deadline rule needs both. Ask the case type next, such as a fall or a dog bite, and open only the questions that type needs.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give each person and company involved a field of their own, including the other side's insurer. Your conflict search runs on clean names, and the intake should wait for that result before anyone books a consultation.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List each doctor and clinic as its own row, with the first visit date and the amount billed so far. Add a field for earlier injuries to the same part of the body, because the attorney will ask about them on the first call.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the questions, the deadline rule for your state and the alert thresholds into the prompt. Emergent builds the form with its database and alerts by Slack or email. When the firm takes on a new case type, prompt again.
fields.howto_step_6_des: End with your firm's wording on what submitting the form does and does not do, followed by a required checkbox. Have an attorney at the firm approve that wording before the form is published on the website.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before the link goes live, submit a fall with fewer than 90 days left and a crash that names a current client. Add a work injury involving another company. Check that each one lands with the right person.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is printable questionnaires from injury firms (a Texas firm's PDF that asks for five years of prior treatment, a Cerritos chiropractor's two-sided sheet, a Scribd sample), one AI template site and a Westlaw malpractice checklist. Every one collects the incident, the injuries and the insurer on paper and leaves the work to a paralegal. This page treats the personal injury intake form as the first day of the case file: the incident date becomes a filing deadline that counts down, every named driver or owner runs against the client list before a consult, each treating provider becomes a row with its bill, and an injury at work is sorted by who else was involved.
tab_stories: A woman who slipped in a grocery aisle enters the date of her fall on a Texas firm's intake, the form saves her two-year filing deadline and shows 61 days left, and because the firm flags anything under 90 days the lead attorney hears in Slack within the hour.

A driver rear-ended at a light names the other driver and his insurer, the conflict search finds that the other driver is a current client of the firm in an unrelated matter, and the intake is held for the managing partner before anyone calls back.

A man bitten by a neighbor's dog lists the emergency room, an urgent care follow-up and a plastic surgery consult with their bills, the form totals $3,950 and gives the paralegal one records request per provider.

A warehouse worker hurt on the job says a delivery driver from another company backed into him, so the intake goes to the injury team as well as the workers' comp group, while a coworker hurt with no outside party involved goes to workers' comp alone.
